answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring each account to lock a stake before trading, then choosing counterparties through a rotating random thread of prior interactions. Random audits compare submitted work with outcomes and neighboring reports; agents that perform consistently keep their stake and gain access, while attempts to forge evidence or coordinate duplicate accounts lose the bond and reputation. A sybil attacker must finance every fake identity and repeatedly risk capital, while honest agents cultivate an orchard of reliable relationships.
